project.bridge.title: Build a Bridge
project.bridge.story: A toy car needs to cross the gap. Can you build a way across?
project.bridge.mission: Build a bridge that holds the toy car
project.bridge.safety: Ask a grown-up before testing with real objects.
step.bridge.j1.prompt: Look at the gap. What could we put across it?
step.bridge.j1.parent: Ask what your child notices about the gap. There is no right answer yet.
step.bridge.j2.prompt: Put pieces down and test the bridge with the car.
step.bridge.j2.parent: Your child places pieces by tapping. At home the same idea works: a plank across two stacks of books.
step.bridge.j3.prompt: Drive the car across. Did it hold?
step.bridge.j3.parent: Count the tries together. A test that stops is information, not a mistake.
step.bridge.j4.prompt: Build it a different way, then test again!
step.bridge.j4.parent: At home, fold a paper bridge a different way and test it again — a grown-up sets up the 15 cm gap first.
step.bridge.j5.prompt: Show your bridge to a grown-up. Tell them how you built it.
step.bridge.j5.parent: Drawing the bridge at home counts as the artifact. Ask your child to point out each part.
step.bridge.e1.prompt: A bridge carries the load to its pillars. Which design will hold more, and why?
step.bridge.e1.parent: Ask for a prediction before any testing. Guessing first makes the result meaningful.
step.bridge.e2.prompt: Build your first bridge so it reaches both sides.
step.bridge.e2.parent: Three designs to try at home with paper and tape: flat sheet, folded sheet, and a triangle or tube (20 cm gap, set up by a grown-up).
step.bridge.e3.prompt: Test it. What happened when the car crossed?
step.bridge.e3.parent: Coins work as weights from age 6 with a grown-up nearby. Record each result together.
step.bridge.e4.prompt: Change one thing, then test again.
step.bridge.e4.parent: A fair test changes only one thing — for example, tape at the joints.
step.bridge.e5.prompt: Say it out loud: My bridge held because…
step.bridge.e5.parent: Ask for the full sentence: My bridge held ___ because ___. The reason matters more than the number.
step.bridge.m1.prompt: Strong bridges use triangles. Where can you add a brace?
step.bridge.m1.parent: At home, measure the gap in centimeters with a ruler before building (25 cm for Maker).
step.bridge.m2.prompt: Build within the budget and test with the car.
step.bridge.m2.parent: Budget check: wood is cheaper, steel is stronger. Ask what they gave up to save coins.
step.bridge.m3.prompt: Test it, then read the log. How much did it hold?
step.bridge.m3.parent: Record three trials in a table — the Bridge Log. Numbers beat memory.
step.bridge.m4.prompt: Change one variable and run three tests.
step.bridge.m4.parent: Change one variable only: shape or number of layers, never both.
step.bridge.m5.prompt: What did you learn? What would you improve? Tell a grown-up.
step.bridge.m5.parent: A full report at home: a photo, the log table, and three sentences on what they learned and would improve.
hints.bridge.j1.1: What is between the two sides?
hints.bridge.j1.4: Watch me put one plank across the gap.
hints.bridge.j1.5: A flat plank rests on both sides, so it can cross the gap.
hints.bridge.j2.1: What happened when the car drove on it?
hints.bridge.j2.3: Add two more pieces under the top.
hints.bridge.j2.4: Watch how I place pieces side by side.
hints.bridge.j2.5: Pieces side by side hold the weight together.
hints.bridge.j3.1: Where do you think the car will go?
hints.bridge.j3.2: Press Test and watch the whole bridge.
hints.bridge.j3.3: Watch the middle of the bridge closely.
hints.bridge.j3.4: Watch the car cross without falling.
hints.bridge.j3.5: The bridge holds the car up while it crosses.
hints.bridge.j4.2: Try a different shape on top.
hints.bridge.j4.4: Watch me change one part, then test.
hints.bridge.j4.5: Changing one thing shows what makes it stronger.
hints.bridge.j5.2: Point to the parts of your bridge.
hints.bridge.j5.3: Tell them which part was hardest.
hints.bridge.j5.4: Watch me tell a grown-up about my bridge.
hints.bridge.j5.5: Your bridge works because the pieces hold it up.
hints.bridge.e1.1: Where does the car's weight go?
hints.bridge.e1.3: Put a pillar under each end.
hints.bridge.e1.4: Watch the load travel down to the pillars.
hints.bridge.e1.5: The load travels down through the pillars into the ground.
hints.bridge.e2.1: Where will your bridge touch both sides?
hints.bridge.e2.2: Put one plank on each side first.
hints.bridge.e2.3: Join the two sides with a beam.
hints.bridge.e2.4: Watch me join both sides, then test.
hints.bridge.e2.5: A bridge rests on both sides of the gap.
hints.bridge.e3.1: What do you see when it breaks?
hints.bridge.e3.3: Try a pillar in the middle.
hints.bridge.e3.4: Watch me add a middle pillar.
hints.bridge.e3.5: The middle sags when it cannot carry the load. A pillar carries it down.
hints.bridge.e4.1: What is one thing you could change?
hints.bridge.e4.2: Change only one thing, for example the joints.
hints.bridge.e4.3: Add a brace at the joint.
hints.bridge.e4.4: Watch me change one thing, then test again.
hints.bridge.e4.5: Changing one thing at a time shows what really helped.
hints.bridge.e5.3: Start with: My bridge held because…
hints.bridge.e5.4: Watch me explain with one reason.
hints.bridge.e5.5: Strong bridges share the load on both sides and carry it down through the pillars.
hints.bridge.m1.1: Which shape is stronger, a square or a triangle?
hints.bridge.m1.4: Watch a diagonal turn a square into triangles.
hints.bridge.m1.5: Triangles keep their shape, so braces stop the bridge from folding.
hints.bridge.m2.1: Did it stay inside the budget?
hints.bridge.m2.2: Wood is cheaper. Steel is stronger.
hints.bridge.m2.4: Watch me balance cost and strength.
hints.bridge.m2.5: Every piece spends coins. Spend them where the load is heaviest.
hints.bridge.m3.1: What do you expect when you press Test?
hints.bridge.m3.2: Watch the test log after the run.
hints.bridge.m3.3: Look at where the load is highest.
hints.bridge.m3.4: Watch me run a test and read the log.
hints.bridge.m3.5: The log shows how much the bridge held and when it failed.
hints.bridge.m4.1: Which one variable will you change?
hints.bridge.m4.2: Change the shape or the number of layers, not both.
hints.bridge.m4.3: Run the test three times for a fair result.
hints.bridge.m4.4: Watch me change one variable and run three tests.
hints.bridge.m4.5: Three trials with one change show a pattern you can trust.
hints.bridge.m5.1: What did your bridge do well?
hints.bridge.m5.2: Use the numbers from your test log.
hints.bridge.m5.3: Say what you learned in one sentence.
hints.bridge.m5.4: Watch me explain what I would improve.
hints.bridge.m5.5: A good report says what you changed, what happened, and why.
